title: Asiya and Maryam
hook: two women set as examples for all believers: Pharaoh's wife and Maryam (66:11–12)

segments.voice: Yesterday: sincere repentance, tawbatan nasuha. Your line was turn back sincerely. Did an apology come out the real way? Today, the same surah ends with two women. Day six hundred thirty-five.

Picture the richest house in Egypt. Gold on the walls, servants in every corridor, a husband who calls himself a god. His wife has everything a palace can give. And one day she asks for a house. Not a bigger palace. A different house, somewhere else entirely. The last verses of surah at-Tahrim hold up two women as examples, and the Qur'an says they are examples for everyone who believes, men and women alike. One is the wife of Pharaoh. The other is Maryam.

Verse eleven, in Pickthall: "And Allah citeth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh when she said: My Lord! Build for me a home with Thee in the Garden." The verse goes on: and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds. The Qur'an never gives her name. The name Asiya comes from the hadith. And she's the same woman who, in surah al-Qasas, looked at a baby pulled from the river and said: don't kill him, he may be a comfort to us. That baby was Musa. Now look at the order of her prayer. A home with Thee, then in the Garden. Commentators noticed that she asks for the neighbor before the house: near You first, then where. Arabic speakers have an old saying for it, al-jar qabl ad-dar, the neighbor before the house. She was married to the most powerful man on earth and asked to live near Someone else. Verse twelve turns to Maryam, daughter of 'Imran: she guarded her chastity, she believed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devout. Maryam, the mother of 'Isa, is the only woman named in the Qur'an, and a whole surah carries her name. And a hadith in Bukhari says that among women, Maryam and Asiya reached perfection. So the surah ends here: one woman inside the house of a tyrant, one woman alone, both held up for every believer to learn from. Neither had a husband who shared her faith. Each found her nearness to Allah anyway.

The practice: Asiya's prayer, a house near You. If you pray, you can say her words from the verse, my Lord, build for me a home with Thee in the Garden, slowly, once or a few times. If you don't, try the picture instead. Think of the place you feel most yourself, and notice what makes it home: the walls, or who is near. Sit with that. Let the house fade and the nearness stay. The bell holds the time.
Asiya and Maryam. Pharaoh's wife, who asked for a home near Allah, and Maryam, who believed her Lord's words: two examples, says 66:11–12, for all believers. Today's word.
Your line: a house near you. Today, when you walk into your home, pause at the door for one breath and ask what would make it near to what matters. Day six hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Many Muslims memorize and pray Asiya's words from 66:11, asking for a home near Allah in the Garden, and honor her and Maryam among the best of women, as hadith describe them.

original.note: Arabic, 66:11: build for me, with You, a house in the Garden. 'with You' comes before 'a house'.

trapdoor: what you thought: two holy women from old stories.
what it means: a queen in a tyrant's house and a woman alone, both set as examples for every believer.
what a scholar hears: in 66:11 'indaka, with You, comes before baytan, a house: the neighbor before the house.
